finding: At 1× Geth is ~3.3× slower from a single NM peer. At 3.5× the trade-off flips two ways: NM finishes ~4 h sooner (it drains the storage-spam mega-tries as a clean final phase, while Geth front-loads them and stalls stop-go on each one), but Geth is far leaner on memory (~6.7 GB peak vs NM's ~18.4 GB). Every run reconstructs the source state root bit-for-bit.
caveat: Wall time and bandwidth are single-dedicated-peer, controlled-LAN figures — read as relative scaling across state sizes, not real-world multi-peer sync time. DB size and peak RSS are topology-independent. Source states are frozen; NM uses the additive Sync.StaticSnapPivot flag (nethermind#11943), Geth a minimal fake-CL forkchoice. 5× / 7× / 10× snap-sync pending (issues #16 / #17 / #18).
